title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows: Facilitator AI notes for in-person meetings
notes: claim 71: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing calls the room's Loop prerequisite unconfirmed even though Microsoft's tenant notice explicitly names both required settings, and it overlooks documented SharePoint storage quota consumption. The app-blocking command also needs correction or removal because its reference gives inconsistent syntax and describes the printed example as unblocking an app.

claims.claim: Facilitator already takes notes in scheduled Teams meetings.
claims.quote: Facilitator is an AI-powered agent in Teams that can automatically take notes of the conversations that happen during a meeting, provide key highlights, and answer prompts in the meeting chat.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Facilitator supports unscheduled in-person discussions in Teams Rooms.
claims.quote: Facilitator in Teams Rooms: Used for unscheduled in-person discussions with a Teams Room device available in the meeting room.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Someone starts Facilitator by tapping Take notes on the console or touch board home screen.
claims.quote: Facilitator in Teams Rooms can be initiated by tapping on the “Take notes” button on the home screen of the console or touch board.

claims.claim: Facilitator captures notes, decisions and action items for in-person meetings.
claims.quote: This enhancement allows teams meeting in a physical room to capture real-time notes, decisions, and action items—without requiring a scheduled or hybrid meeting.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Generated notes appear on the front-of-room display as participants speak, exposing them to people in the room.
claims.quote: Notes can take a few minutes to generate and appear on the front-of-room display as participants speak.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: At the end of the session participants select Save notes and add participant names so those people can access the notes and transcript later.
claims.quote: At the end of the session, select Save notes and ensure participants’ names are added in the dialog pop-up so they can access the notes and transcript later on their personal devices.

claims.claim: Unsaved notes are deleted after the session ends.
claims.quote: Unsaved notes are deleted after the session ends.

claims.claim: Participants access the notes and transcript on Teams desktop through the Recap tab of the chat titled Meeting with [conference room name].
claims.quote: To access notes after the meeting, navigate to the Teams meeting chat titled “Meeting with [conference room name].” At the top of the meeting chat, select the Recap tab, and then select Notes to find the AI-generated notes and transcript.

claims.claim: Facilitator turns on transcription but does not record the meeting.
claims.quote: Facilitator only turns on transcription during the meeting. The meeting won't be recorded.

claims.claim: Muting the room microphone prevents Facilitator or transcription capturing content.
claims.quote: You can mute the microphone in the room to ensure Facilitator or transcription doesn't capture any content.

claims.claim: Only participants who add their names at the beginning and have enrolled profiles are identified and attributed in notes and transcription.
claims.quote: Currently, only participants who add their names at the beginning of the meeting session will be identified and attributed, provided that they have enrolled their profiles.

claims.quote: No meeting data is stored or cached on the Teams Rooms device after the meeting ends.

claims.claim: The stored data is treated as meeting transcript data.

claims.claim: The per-room button setting is in Teams Rooms Pro Management portal > Rooms > room > Settings > Device > Show Take notes button on the home screen.
claims.quote: In Pro Management portal, select Rooms from the left navigation > select your desired room > Settings > Device > Show Take notes button on the home screen.

claims.claim: Show Take notes button on the home screen is enabled by default.
claims.quote: Show Take notes button on the home screen. The default setting is enabled.

claims.claim: Pro Management portal device configuration requires Rooms Management RBAC permissions.
claims.quote: you can configure settings for Microsoft Teams devices (Teams Rooms on Windows, Teams Rooms on Android, Teams Panels and Teams Phones), provided you have the necessary role-based access control permissions for Rooms Management.

claims.claim: No API or automation equivalent for the room's Take notes home-screen button is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Facilitator Take notes button PowerShell Graph XML configuration home screen; "Teams Rooms" "Take notes" "Graph" "PowerShell". Opened rooms/facilitator-teams-rooms, rooms/pro-portal-settings and rooms/xml-config-file; no matching automation setting.

claims.claim: Facilitator is allowed or blocked through Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > actions menu > Allow or Block.
claims.quote:
select Teams apps > Manage apps.
3. In the apps list's search box, search for Facilitator.
4. Select Facilitator from the app list.
5. In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: Facilitator is allowed by default.
claims.quote: Facilitator is allowed by default. However, if all apps are blocked for your organization, Facilitator is also blocked.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <Facilitator app ID> -IsBlocked $true is a documented runnable command to block Facilitator.
claims.quote: Searched: Update-M365TeamsApp IsBlocked true block app. Opened microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp: Example 3 prints this call but says 'Unblocks Bookings app'; syntax and parameter tables require additional arguments. The reference does not unambiguously support this blocking instruction.
claims.fix: Remove the printed Update-M365TeamsApp blocking command from controls[1].api and the rendered table; retain the verified Teams admin center Allow or Block path. State in the row note: 'The Update-M365TeamsApp reference is internally inconsistent about the example and required parameters, so no blocking call is provided here.'

go to Meetings > Meeting policies.

claims.claim: The SharePoint collaborative meeting notes setting applies to the whole tenant and cannot be configured per user.
claims.quote: This property controls the collaborative meeting notes creation and integration in Microsoft Teams. It applies to the entire tenant and can't be configured at the user level.

claims.claim: The SharePoint property does not apply to collaborative meeting notes in Teams New Calendar, which uses Cloud Policy settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed whether the SharePoint Loop settings or Cloud Policy govern room notes.
claims.quote: Verify Loop components are enabled:- IsLoopEnabled- IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled
claims.fix: Replace 'Which one governs room notes is not confirmed' in the row note and corresponding prose/question with: 'MC1307512 explicitly requires IsLoopEnabled and IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled for in-person room notes. Cloud Policy is documented for Teams New Calendar, not as a substitute for those room prerequisites.' Retain the general Cloud Policy path only with that qualification.

claims.claim: MC1307512 specifically asks administrators to verify IsLoopEnabled and IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled.

claims.quote: Facilitator's AI-generated notes for meetings aren't automatically collected as cloud attachments in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery because it isn't currently supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The sources do not explicitly resolve application of those meeting-note limitations to the distinct in-person room-note storage scenario.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Facilitator in-person notes sensitivity labels eDiscovery watermarks meeting policy IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled. Opened rooms/facilitator-teams-rooms, facilitator-teams and purview/ai-teams-facilitator; none explicitly resolves these limits for in-person room notes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The sources do not describe an announcement notifying in-room participants that this transcription has started.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Facilitator in-person notes transcription notification announcement prerequisites missing button. Opened rooms/facilitator-teams-rooms and meeting-transcription-captions; read MC1307512. Search returned general notification guidance, not an in-person Facilitator announcement.

claims.claim: No other trigger for starting unscheduled in-person notes is described on the sources read.
claims.quote: Searched: "Facilitator" "in-person" "automatically" "start". Opened rooms/facilitator-teams-rooms and rooms/rooms-release-note; read MC1307512. These describe tapping Take notes, not an alternative automatic trigger for unscheduled room notes.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not describe the Take notes button's behaviour when a prerequisite is missing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Facilitator in-person notes transcription notification announcement prerequisites missing button. Opened rooms/facilitator-teams-rooms and facilitator-teams; read MC1307512. Prerequisites are listed, but no missing-prerequisite button behaviour is specified.

claims.claim: No dedicated single tenant switch specific to in-person room notes is documented beyond the listed existing prerequisites and per-room button setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Facilitator" "in-person" "tenant" "switch". Opened rooms/facilitator-teams-rooms and facilitator-teams; read MC1307512. They document the app, Loop, transcription and room setting, not a separate dedicated tenant switch for this scenario.

claims.claim: The cited feature documentation states no feature-specific meter, credit rate or usage charge.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Facilitator in-person notes licensing meter credits SharePoint Embedded storage quota cost. Opened rooms/facilitator-teams-rooms, facilitator-teams, rooms/rooms-licensing and loop/loop-storage. No room-note-specific meter or credit rate was stated.

claims.claim: The briefing's cited pages do not give the price of Teams Rooms Pro.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Facilitator in-person notes licensing meter credits SharePoint Embedded storage quota cost. Opened rooms/facilitator-teams-rooms, facilitator-teams and rooms/rooms-licensing; the cited setup and policy pages give no Teams Rooms Pro price.

claims.claim: The cited feature documentation does not publish what a future licensing-model change would cost.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Facilitator in-person notes licensing meter credits SharePoint Embedded storage quota cost. Opened rooms/facilitator-teams-rooms and rooms/rooms-licensing. The feature page warns the model may change but supplies no replacement model or future price.

claims.claim: No quota is stated on the cited pages for the saved notes' Loop storage.
claims.quote: Loop components and their integrations are powered by .loop files (earlier releases created .fluid files), stored in OneDrive, SharePoint, or SharePoint Embedded. Storage counts against your organization's SharePoint quota.
claims.fix: Replace 'SharePoint Embedded storage for saved notes, for which no quota or charge is stated on the pages read' with 'SharePoint storage quota consumed by saved Loop notes; the cited Loop admin policy page says Loop storage counts against the organisation's SharePoint quota.' Do not add a room-specific storage price or numeric allowance.

claims.claim: The in-person room scenario's setup steps name no Microsoft 365 Copilot licence prerequisite.
claims.quote: Pre-requisite: Assign a Teams Rooms Pro license to each resource account you have for your Teams Rooms devices

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist names controls that lack their own representation in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Assign a Teams Rooms Pro licence' and 'Loop settings IsLoopEnabled and IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled'. Table: button, Facilitator app, transcription and collaborative meeting notes; no licence-assignment or IsLoopEnabled control.

claims.claim: Users elsewhere are not affected by this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Facilitator" "room" "notes" "access" "participants". Opened rooms/facilitator-teams-rooms; read MC1307512. Sources describe later access on personal devices but do not state that users outside Pro-licensed rooms are unaffected.
claims.fix: Remove '; users elsewhere are not affected' from the impact rationale. Retain the supported sentence about the new entry point and front-of-room notes display.
